papers.title: Gene-specific machine learning model EpiPred identifies likely pathogenic variants in the epilepsy-related gene STXBP1.
papers.abstract: STXBP1 variants are a frequent cause of early-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathies and related neurodevelopmental disorders, but the clinical interpretation of these variants remains a major challenge. Most reported STXBP1 missense variants are classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS), complicating diagnosis, counseling, and patient eligibility for precision therapies. Here, we developed EpiPred, a gene-specific machine learning classifier that predicts the pathogenicity of STXBP1 missense variants and tests these predictions using empirical evidence from well-estab
papers.summary: The authors developed EpiPred, a gene-specific machine learning classifier that predicts whether missense variants in the epilepsy-related gene STXBP1 are pathogenic or benign. This addresses the common problem of variants of uncertain significance (VUS) that complicate diagnosis and treatment decisions for patients with STXBP1-related neurodevelopmental disorders. The model's predictions were validated against empirical functional evidence.

papers.title: Early Clinical and Cerebrospinal Fluid Predictors of 1-Year Recurrence in Autoimmune GFAP Astrocytopathy.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune glial fibrillary acidic protein astrocytopathy (GFAP-A) is an inflammatory central nervous system disorder with variable outcomes. Relapse occurs in a subset of patients, but early predictors remain unclear. We aimed to identify admission-available features associated with 1-year recurrence and develop an interpretable risk stratification model.
papers.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
papers.summary: This study investigates which clinical and cerebrospinal fluid features available at hospital admission can predict relapse within one year in patients with autoimmune GFAP astrocytopathy, a rare inflammatory CNS disorder. The authors aim to build an interpretable risk stratification model to help clinicians identify high-risk patients early.

papers.title: Multimodal AI and single-cell transcriptomics integrate to construct a histopathological prognostic model for bladder cancer, revealing the RTN3-glycolysis axis in chemoresistance.
papers.abstract: Bladder cancer is a common malignant tumor of the urinary system, and gemcitabine-based chemotherapy often fails because of drug resistance. Tumor heterogeneity, particularly copy number variations (CNVs) heterogeneity at the genomic level, is a core factor that drives disease progression and drug resistance. However, the relationship between CNV heterogeneity at the single-cell level and the histomorphological features that are relied upon in a routine pathological diagnosis remains unclear, limiting its application in clinical prognostic assessments and precision therapy.
papers.summary: This study combines multimodal AI with single-cell transcriptomics to build a histopathological prognostic model for bladder cancer, linking genomic copy number variation heterogeneity to tissue morphology. The model identifies an RTN3-glycolysis axis as a driver of gemcitabine chemoresistance, offering a potential biomarker and therapeutic target. The work demonstrates how integrating imaging and single-cell data can bridge routine pathology with molecular mechanisms.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Culture-Confirmed Neonatal Sepsis in a Tertiary Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Neonatal sepsis remains a major cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Early diagnosis is challenging because of nonspecific clinical manifestations and delays in laboratory confirmation. Machine learning (ML) approaches using structured electronic health record (EHR) data may improve early risk stratification in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs).
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study developed machine learning models using structured electronic health record data to predict culture-confirmed neonatal sepsis in a tertiary NICU. The work aims to improve early risk stratification in settings where diagnosis is delayed by nonspecific symptoms and slow laboratory confirmation, particularly in low- and middle-income countries.

papers.title: EmmaEmb: A quantitative framework for analyzing embedding spaces in molecular biology.
papers.abstract: Embeddings, numerical vectors learned by deep-learning models, are increasingly used to represent complex molecular biology data and support predictive tasks and generative design. There is a growing need for systematic approaches to interpret and explain the information encoded in high-dimensional embedding spaces. Here, we introduce EmmaEmb, a quantitative, model-agnostic framework for geometric correction, direct analysis, and comparison of embedding spaces. Our framework encompasses local and global analysis methods to quantify data distribution within an embedding space and enable compari
papers.summary: EmmaEmb is a model-agnostic framework for quantitatively analyzing and comparing embedding spaces in molecular biology, offering geometric correction and both local and global analysis methods. It enables systematic interpretation of what information deep-learning embeddings encode, addressing a growing need for explainability in molecular representation learning.

papers.title: An interpretable framework applying protein words to predict protein-small molecule complementary pairing rules.
papers.abstract: Despite the high accuracy of 'black box' deep learning models, drug discovery still relies on protein-ligand interaction principles and heuristics. To improve interpretability of protein-small molecule binding predictions, we developed the PWRules framework, which applies binding affinity data to identify privileged small molecule fragments and subsequently defines complementary pairing rules between these fragments and protein words (semantic sequence units) through an interpretability module. The resulting word-fragment rules are then used by the PWScore function to prioritize active compoun
papers.summary: The authors present PWRules, an interpretable framework that learns 'protein words' (semantic sequence units) and pairs them with privileged small-molecule fragments using binding affinity data, yielding explicit complementary pairing rules. A scoring function, PWScore, then uses these rules to prioritize active compounds, offering a transparent alternative to black-box deep learning models in drug discovery.

papers.title: Residual-Guided Hybrid Stochastic Modeling: A Two-Stage Learning Framework for Urban GNSS Positioning Enhancement.
papers.abstract: The Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) has been widely adopted in navigation applications due to its high accuracy and convenience. However, in urban canyon environments, severe signal blockage caused by buildings and trees introduces substantial non-line-of-sight errors and multipath effects, leading to degraded and highly fluctuating positioning performance. To address this issue, this paper proposes a residual-guided hybrid stochastic modeling framework. The method operates in two stages: first, a pseudo-range correction estimation network takes GNSS parameters containing residuals a
papers.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage learning framework for improving GNSS positioning accuracy in urban environments, where buildings and trees cause signal blockage, non-line-of-sight errors, and multipath effects. The first stage uses a neural network to estimate pseudo-range corrections from GNSS parameters containing residuals, and the second stage applies hybrid stochastic modeling to refine positioning. The approach aims to reduce the large, fluctuating errors that degrade navigation performance in urban canyons.

papers.title: Quality Variation Patterns and Predictive Modeling of Fermented Soybean Whey-Based Tofu Under Cold-Chain Conditions Using Kinetic and Machine Learning Approaches.
papers.abstract: Pre-packaged fermented soybean whey-based tofu (FSW-tofu) was stored under dynamic temperature conditions (4-20 °C) that simulated typical supermarket and e-commerce cold-chain transport modes. Changes in total viable count (TVC), psychrophilic bacterial count (PBC), hardness, springiness, chewiness, and water-holding capacity were monitored over 35 d, and a hybrid prediction model integrating mechanistic kinetics with machine learning was established. Results indicated that both temperature fluctuation amplitude and frequency significantly affected microbial proliferation and textural degrada
papers.summary: This study monitored how pre-packaged fermented soybean whey-based tofu degrades under simulated cold-chain temperature fluctuations (4-20 °C) over 35 days, tracking microbial counts and texture properties. The authors built a hybrid model combining mechanistic kinetics with machine learning to predict quality changes, finding that both the amplitude and frequency of temperature fluctuations significantly affect microbial growth and textural degradation.

papers.title: Phage bioinformatics tools: a review of computational approaches for bacteriophage research.
papers.abstract: Rising clinical interest in phage therapy and the exponential growth of metagenomic sequence catalogues have driven a rapid expansion of bacteriophage bioinformatics. More than 80 dedicated tools, mostly published since 2020, now span identification, assembly, annotation, taxonomy, lifestyle prediction, defence-system detection, and host prediction. Aimed at experienced practitioners and developers, this review synthesizes the field through the lens of three successive computational paradigms: sequence homology, bounded by database completeness; machine learning, constrained by labelled traini
papers.summary: This review surveys over 80 computational tools developed for bacteriophage research, most published since 2020, covering tasks such as phage identification, assembly, annotation, taxonomy, lifestyle prediction, defence-system detection, and host prediction. It organizes the field around three successive computational paradigms—sequence homology, machine learning, and emerging approaches—and discusses the limitations each faces, such as database completeness and labelled training data constraints.

papers.title: HighFold4: extending AlphaFold3 to accurate cyclic peptide conformation prediction via custom chemical connectivity.
papers.abstract: While AlphaFold3 has revolutionized protein structure prediction and supports noncanonical amino acids, its architecture always fails to reliably generate the closed-ring topologies characteristic of cyclic peptides. Existing adaptations, such as imposing distance constraints via an offset matrix, enforce ring geometry but cannot specify the chemical identity of the cyclization bond, leading to a restrictive bias toward amide- or disulfide-linked macrocycles. Here, we present HighFold4, a framework that adapts AlphaFold3 to explicitly incorporate user-defined chemical connectivity between resi
papers.summary: HighFold4 extends AlphaFold3 to accurately predict cyclic peptide conformations by explicitly encoding user-defined chemical connectivity for cyclization bonds, rather than relying on distance constraints that bias predictions toward amide- or disulfide-linked macrocycles. This allows reliable modeling of diverse closed-ring topologies that AlphaFold3 alone cannot generate.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omics and Radiogenomic Analysis Identifies S100B and ITGB5 as Complementary Candidate Biomarkers of Glioblastoma Heterogeneity.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by marked intratumoral heterogeneity, diffuse invasion, and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In this study, we applied an integrative multi-omics and radiogenomic framework to identify candidate biomarkers reflecting complementary dimensions of GBM heterogeneity. Public bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated to define GBM-related differentially expressed genes, which were intersected with curated microbiota-associated gene sets as a hypothesis-generating screening strategy. Machine-learning models with SHAP interpretation were use
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomic data with radiogenomic and microbiota-associated gene sets to identify candidate biomarkers of glioblastoma heterogeneity, nominating S100B and ITGB5 as complementary markers. Machine-learning models with SHAP interpretation were used to prioritize these genes, though the microbiota-based screening approach is hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory.

papers.title: Predicting non-specific binding of VHHs using machine learning models with cluster-aware validation.
papers.abstract: Propensity for nonspecific binding-also known as polyreactivity-is a serious developability risk factor for biotherapeutic candidates. To minimize this risk, drug companies are increasingly relying on in silico tools utilizing machine learning methods, but developing these tools is challenging. For example, the available data often contains many closely related sequences originating from drug pipeline projects, which can introduce significant biases in the in silico models training and benchmarking, leading to poor generalizability on new data. We present here a workflow designed to diagnose a
papers.summary: This paper presents a machine learning workflow for predicting non-specific binding (polyreactivity) of VHH antibody fragments, a key developability risk for biotherapeutics. The authors emphasize that standard random train-test splits are misleading because datasets contain many closely related sequences from drug pipelines, so they introduce cluster-aware validation to better assess true generalizability. This approach provides a more realistic benchmark for in silico developability tools.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Multi-Fidelity Graph Learning for Sequence-Aware Residual Bolt Preload Prediction in Hyperelastic-Sealed Flanges.
papers.abstract: Sequential tightening redistributes load among bolts and produces a residual preload field that depends on the complete operation history. This study presents a physics-informed graph-learning framework for a 60-bolt circular flange. The model receives initial preloads and tightening order and predicts the residual preload field on a complete causal directed graph. All 1770 admissible later-to-earlier edges are retained. Among them, 240 local edges carry non-zero Elastic Interaction Coefficient Method (EICM) attributes, while 1530 distant edges remain available to learned message passing. The
papers.summary: This paper develops a physics-informed graph-learning framework to predict residual bolt preload in a 60-bolt hyperelastic-sealed flange, accounting for the full sequential tightening history. The model combines known elastic interaction coefficients on local edges with learned message passing on distant edges, using a causal directed graph. It demonstrates a multi-fidelity approach that blends physical priors with data-driven learning for engineering preload prediction.

papers.title: PMAVP: A Mamba-Inspired Deep Learning Framework for Antiviral Peptide Identification and Functional Activity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate computational prediction of antiviral peptides (AVPs) can accelerate peptide screening and reduce experimental costs. However, existing deep learning-based methods still suffer from severe class imbalance, over-reliance on handcrafted features and limited interpretability. Here, we propose PMAVP, a multi-task learning framework that integrates the ProtT5 pre-trained protein language model with a Mamba-inspired module for AVP identification and functional activity prediction. We use ProtT5 to extract deep semantic representations from peptide sequences and a Mamba module to capture lon
papers.summary: PMAVP is a multi-task deep learning framework that combines the ProtT5 protein language model with a Mamba-inspired sequence module to identify antiviral peptides and predict their functional activity. It aims to address class imbalance, reliance on handcrafted features, and limited interpretability in prior AVP prediction methods. The approach could speed up computational screening of antiviral peptides and reduce experimental costs.

papers.title: Understanding Human Motion from Depth Sensors: Activity Recognition and Age Group Recognition Using Skeleton Data.
papers.abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) plays a significant role in various applications, from learning a discipline to physical rehabilitation. In older adults, activity patterns can indicate levels of frailty, which helps inform the design of physical training programs to prevent falls and maintain mobility. HAR sensing ranges from wearable sensors such as IMUs and RGB cameras to video, specialized gait laboratories, perturbation units, VR, and other modalities. This paper presents a comprehensive study of depth-based, skeleton-driven HAR and age group recognition (AGR) using data collected from re
papers.summary: This paper presents a study using depth-sensor skeleton data to recognize human activities and classify age groups, with a focus on applications like frailty assessment and fall prevention in older adults. It compares depth-based sensing to other modalities such as wearables and cameras for activity recognition.

papers.title: Relative Humidity Shifts During Evaporation Enhance the Donor Differentiation Potential of Serum and Plasma Dried Droplet Patterns.
papers.abstract: The droplet evaporation method (DEM) is an analytical approach in which substances dissolved or suspended in a liquid self-assemble into characteristic patterns upon evaporation. Applied to blood and blood-derived fluids, DEM has shown potential for diagnostics. In a previous study, we identified optimal temperature and relative humidity (rH) conditions for generating two main pattern features in dried serum and plasma droplets: crystalline structures (favored at high rH) and peripheral cracks (favored at low rH). The aim of the present study was to investigate whether sequential exposure to t
papers.summary: This study investigates how changing relative humidity during the evaporation of serum and plasma droplets affects the resulting dried patterns, specifically the balance between crystalline structures and peripheral cracks. The authors find that shifting humidity conditions can enhance the differentiation potential of these patterns, which may improve the diagnostic utility of the droplet evaporation method.

papers.title: Construction of a Neoantigen Prognostic Model for Gastric Adenocarcinoma Based on Multi-Omics Data Mining and the Design of mRNA Vaccines and Targeted Drugs.
papers.abstract: This study systematically explored immune targets in gastric adenocarcinoma (GAC) suitable for mRNA vaccine development. Based on multi-omics data from public databases, we first screened a set of potential tumor-associated antigen genes. Subsequently, using ten machine learning algorithms, we constructed 101 prognostic models and, through optimization and comparison, selected the Random Survival Forest (RSF) method to establish a clinical prognostic model for GAC consisting of seven genes (TYMP, IFGN, ITGAX, GBP5, GBP4, STAT1, CD84). At both the genetic and protein levels, these genes were cl
papers.summary: This study mined multi-omics data from public databases to identify tumor-associated antigens in gastric adenocarcinoma that could serve as targets for mRNA vaccine development. Using ten machine learning algorithms to build 101 prognostic models, the authors selected a Random Survival Forest model based on seven immune-related genes (TYMP, IFGN, ITGAX, GBP5, GBP4, STAT1, CD84) and further designed candidate mRNA vaccines and targeted drugs. The work integrates prognostic modeling with immunotherapeutic design, though it remains a computational study without experimental validation.

papers.title: GDA-Pred: Generative AI-Driven Data Augmentation for Improved Prediction of IL-6 and IL-13-Inducing Peptides.
papers.abstract: Identifying interleukin-6 (IL-6) and interleukin-13 (IL-13)-inducing peptides is important for drug discovery targeting cancer, immune disorders, and infectious diseases. However, experimental screening is costly and time-consuming. Machine learning and deep learning models have been developed that distinguish functional peptides from no-function ones, but their performance is limited by the small number of experimentally validated peptides. In this study, we propose a generative AI-driven data augmentation framework, GDA, and its prediction system, GDA-Pred, to improve the performance of stat
papers.summary: The authors developed GDA-Pred, a generative AI-based data augmentation framework to improve machine learning prediction of peptides that induce IL-6 and IL-13, which are relevant to cancer and immune disorder drug discovery. By generating synthetic peptide data to overcome the scarcity of experimentally validated samples, the approach aims to boost predictive performance over models trained on limited real data.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Deciphering the Plant Cis-Regulatory Code.
papers.abstract: Much of the regulatory information that shapes plant gene expression lies outside protein-coding regions, including many loci associated with agronomic traits. Deep learning models use DNA sequences and multi-omics data to examine components of this cis-regulatory information. This review compares convolutional, Transformer-based and graph architectures used to represent local sequence features, chromatin state and three-dimensional genome organisation. We assess their applications to transcription-factor binding, chromatin accessibility, gene expression, non-coding variant prioritisation and
papers.summary: This review surveys deep learning approaches for decoding plant cis-regulatory information from DNA sequence and multi-omics data. It compares convolutional, Transformer-based, and graph architectures for modeling local sequence features, chromatin state, and 3D genome organization, and assesses their use in predicting transcription-factor binding, chromatin accessibility, gene expression, and prioritizing non-coding variants. The paper is aimed at plant genomics researchers seeking to apply these models to agronomic trait loci.

papers.title: Small Angle Scattering Techniques on In Situ Adsorption Studies: A Comprehensive Review.
papers.abstract: In situ and operando small-angle X-ray and neutron scattering (SAXS and SANS) have become powerful techniques for studying adsorption processes because they provide real-time information that traditional ex situ methods cannot capture. This review examines the use of these techniques in four major material groups: soft matter and polymers, carbon-based materials, biological systems and ceramics. Unlike conventional before-and-after characterization, in situ methods allow researchers to follow structural changes during adsorption as they happen, revealing adsorption kinetics, intermediate state
papers.summary: This review surveys how in situ and operando small-angle X-ray and neutron scattering (SAXS/SANS) are used to study adsorption processes across soft matter, carbon materials, biological systems, and ceramics. It highlights that these real-time methods reveal adsorption kinetics and intermediate structural states that conventional ex situ characterization cannot capture.

papers.title: Multimodal Deep Learning and Foundation Models for Early Detection and Forecasting of Plant Diseases.
papers.abstract: Plant diseases destroy 20-40% of global food production annually, posing a critical threat to food security for a projected population of 9.7 billion by 2050. Conventional diagnostic approaches relying on expert visual assessment are slow, costly, and unsuitable for modern agricultural scales. While deep convolutional neural networks demonstrated early promise, single-modality, image-centric systems consistently fail under real-world field conditions characterized by variable lighting, co-occurring infections, and cultivar diversity. This review synthesizes a decade of progress across four int
papers.summary: This review synthesizes a decade of research on multimodal deep learning and foundation models for plant disease detection and forecasting, arguing that single-modality image-based systems fail under real-world field conditions. It highlights how integrating multiple data types (e.g., imaging, spectral, genomic, environmental) can improve early detection and forecasting to protect global food security.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic Analyses Identify Four Prognosis-Associated Genes in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the malignant tumors with high incidence and mortality rates worldwide. Given the poor prognosis of patients with HCC, it is crucial to explore the molecular mechanisms underlying HCC development and to evaluate prognostic markers. Differential expression analysis followed by univariate Cox, LASSO, and multivariate Cox regression identified four genes (EPO, SOCS2, IL18RAP, and KPNA2), and a Cox-based risk score was evaluated in the TCGA-LIHC cohort and externally in GSE14520 using Kaplan-Meier and time-dependent ROC analyses. Bulk, single-cell, and prot
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data from HCC patients to identify four genes (EPO, SOCS2, IL18RAP, KPNA2) associated with prognosis, building a Cox-based risk score validated in TCGA-LIHC and GSE14520 cohorts. The risk score stratifies patients by survival and provides candidate biomarkers for HCC prognosis.

papers.title: Saliency-Curated Deep Learning for Predicting Receptor Status in Breast Cancer Brain Metastases.
papers.abstract: Background: Breast cancer brain metastases (BCBMs) exhibit notable receptor discordance between primary tumors and metastases, yet obtaining intracranial biopsies is rarely practical. We created an interpretable deep learning radiogenomic model to predict estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) status from MRI scans in BCBM cases. Methods: A total of 241 post-contrast T1-weighted MRIs from 142 patients were analyzed. We developed a mask-free 3D Residual Neural Network (ResNet) ensemble trained directly on cropped, bias-corrected b
papers.summary: This study developed an interpretable deep learning radiogenomic model that predicts ER, PR, and HER2 receptor status in breast cancer brain metastases directly from MRI scans, avoiding the need for invasive intracranial biopsies. Using a mask-free 3D ResNet ensemble trained on 241 post-contrast T1-weighted MRIs from 142 patients, the approach leverages saliency-based curation to improve model interpretability and performance.

papers.title: Mutation-Aware Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Binding Affinity of Nirmatrelvir Analogs Targeting Coronavirus Main Proteases.
papers.abstract: The emergence of resistance-associated mutations in coronavirus main protease (Mpro) poses a significant challenge to the development of broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics. In this study, we improved and accelerated a mutation-aware machine learning (ML) framework to predict the binding score of Nirmatrelvir analogue ligands against wild-type and mutant MERS-CoV Mpro. A library of 15,889 Nirmatrelvir derivatives generated through systematic scaffold modification was docked against the wild-type and five variants of the Mpro, producing a total of 95,334 structural and docking score datasets
papers.summary: This study presents an improved machine learning framework that predicts binding affinity of Nirmatrelvir analogs against wild-type and mutant coronavirus main proteases. By docking 15,889 derivatives against six Mpro variants, they generated over 95,000 docking datasets to train mutation-aware models. The approach aims to accelerate identification of broad-spectrum antivirals that remain effective against resistance mutations.

papers.title: Predictive model for ulcerative colitis therapeutic response using clinical indicators and peripheral blood T-cell subsets.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to integrate clinical indicators with peripheral blood T-cell subsets to develop a prediction model for ulcerative colitis (UC), and to facilitate precise subtyping and individualized treatment decisions.
papers.summary: This study builds a predictive model for how ulcerative colitis patients will respond to therapy by combining routine clinical indicators with measurements of T-cell subsets in peripheral blood. The goal is to enable more precise patient subtyping and individualized treatment decisions.

papers.title: Identification of Wnt/β-catenin- and immune-related genes in hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury using bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, and a murine model.
papers.abstract: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI) is a major complication following liver transplantation (LT), contributing to graft dysfunction and rejection. The roles of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway and immune responses in LT-related HIRI remain incompletely elucidated. This study aimed to screen key genes associated with Wnt/β-catenin signaling scores and immune regulation in HIRI after LT.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics and single-cell RNA sequencing with a murine model to identify genes linked to Wnt/β-catenin signaling and immune regulation in hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury after liver transplantation. The authors screen for key genes associated with Wnt/β-catenin signaling scores and immune responses, aiming to clarify mechanisms underlying graft dysfunction and rejection.

papers.title: Potential hazard assessment of 6PPD-quinone in the context of ulcerative colitis: network toxicology, machine learning, transcriptomic analysis, and preliminary In vivo validation.
papers.abstract: The ubiquitous tire-derived pollutant 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) poses potential systemic health risks, yet its toxicological impact on the intestinal tract, particularly in the context of ulcerative colitis (UC), remains largely unknown. This study aimed to investigate whether 6PPD-Q aggravates DSS-induced colitis and to identify candidate molecular events using integrative computational and experimental approaches.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the tire-derived pollutant 6PPD-quinone worsens ulcerative colitis, using network toxicology, machine learning, and transcriptomic analysis combined with preliminary in vivo validation in a DSS-induced colitis model. The authors identify candidate molecular events linking 6PPD-Q exposure to colitis aggravation, suggesting an environmental risk factor for intestinal inflammation.

papers.title: Decoding the Bone-Eye Axis: Machine Learning for Age-Related Macular Degeneration Risk Prediction.
papers.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss, yet systemic determinants of its risk remain incompletely understood. Bone mineral density (BMD), a marker of skeletal and biological aging, may reflect shared pathways linking systemic and retinal degeneration. We investigated the association between BMD and AMD using a multilayered framework integrating epidemiological analyses, Mendelian randomization (MR), proteomic and metabolomic profiling, machine learning, and an experimental low-BMD model. Across 3 cohorts, including UK Biobank, National Health and
papers.summary: This study investigates whether bone mineral density (BMD) is linked to age-related macular degeneration (AMD) using a multi-layered approach combining epidemiology, Mendelian randomization, proteomics, metabolomics, and machine learning. The findings suggest that BMD, as a marker of biological aging, may share systemic pathways with retinal degeneration, and the authors develop a machine learning model for AMD risk prediction based on these bone-eye axis signals.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning model based on multimodal MRI radiomics for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), the most common neurodegenerative disorder, is a leading cause of cognitive impairment and dementia in older adults. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model using multimodal MRI radiomics for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: This study develops an interpretable machine learning model that combines radiomic features extracted from multimodal MRI to diagnose Alzheimer's disease. The approach aims to improve diagnostic accuracy while providing interpretable outputs that can support clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Neural Turing Machines for efficient natural language summarization: architecture, optimization, and performance analysis.
papers.abstract: Abstractive text summarization remains a fundamental challenge in Natural Language Processing (NLP), particularly for long documents that require models to preserve long-range dependencies and maintain semantic coherence. Although Transformer-based architectures have achieved strong summarization performance, their full self-attention mechanism scales quadratically with sequence length and often requires input truncation in long-context applications.
papers.summary: This paper explores Neural Turing Machines (NTMs) as an alternative to Transformer-based models for abstractive text summarization, aiming to address the quadratic scaling of self-attention that limits long-document processing. It examines architecture design, optimization strategies, and performance trade-offs, though the abstract does not report specific empirical results.
